Rules.Banking: In sets 01–12, finish the five tracks in the printed order. Bank each finished track’s accuracy, then compare the mean of the five percentages with the set’s pass mark. A replay can raise a banked best. Resume at the next unfinished song. If all five are banked below the mark, replay any of them. Award the room move, item and audition once on passing. The next set opens after the previous pass and any required audition choice. The optional keys seat can be left empty. Passing the stadium rolls the credits and ends the story. After the credits, set 13 opens as a post-credits bonus. The Hall of Fame judges one uninterrupted performance of all five songs, and a passing run plays the induction as an epilogue.
Rules.CurrentGigs: The existing gig system runs a set back to back and checks its average accuracy. Leaving abandons that run. Story banking and this manifest are a proposed campaign layer. Free play stays open to every library song. Backyard Party, Club Night, Festival Slot and Arena Headline remain independent side gigs with generated setlists.
Rules.Staging: Each booking has one gig venue under the note highway. The director catches the change in a wide, band or crowd shot at a marked musical section. Keep the action high or to either side of the highway’s lower centre. At song end, advance the venue state even if the director missed the shot. Sets 01–12 restore it on resume. Set 13 carries it only within the current attempt. The first gig uses the hideout basement itself. From then on, the hideout is where the band lives between dates and where the souvenirs accumulate.
Rules.Auditions: An audition offers two written candidates. Choose one for each required seat and adjust their look afterward if desired. Selected members keep their appearance at home and onstage. Leave unfilled seats clear. Fixed guest acts play the indicated session dates. Candidates who took another gig return in the specified wing, opening bill or crowd shot.
Rules.Difficulty: The campaign uses Expert drums. The two numbers on each booking are provisional targets for the median track density in the set, in drum notes per second. Measure each new chart as note count divided by track duration. Openers can sit below the band and closers can go above it. Check the measured medians across bookings when the charts land. The playing notes describe the records’ rhythmic demands. The early acoustic opener especially leaves real space for rests. Kit changes are visual and use the same drum lanes.
Rules.ChartPlanning: All 65 primaries are slated for new campaign charts. Each pair of alternates comes from the saved-song export and fits that slot’s musical or dramatic job. An alternate is an editorial option before a booking ships. If picked, check its density and bind the cue to a section in that recording. The printed primary determines the set time.
Rules.NotesPerSecondMeaning: target range for median of five Expert chart densities
Rules.ChartedMeaning: true when the new campaign drum chart has been authored
Rules.ConditionalSeat: keys joins home-band dates 11, 12 and 13 if selected

Sets.Title: In the Basement with My AirPods
Sets.VenueWork: Use the built hideout basement as the playable room. Dress the existing bucket, camcorder, CRT, window well and kitchen stairs.
Sets.KitLook: Hand-me-down kit on the carpet offcut
Sets.Premise: The old bucket drums are still beside the real kit. Upstairs somebody leaves the kitchen door open a little longer with each song. Down here it’s just you, the camcorder and the BASSIST WANTED flyer on the gig board.

Songs.Title: Royals
Songs.PlayingNote: A low pulse and spaced handclaps leave the vocal plenty of room.

Cue.Do: The camcorder’s red tally lamp comes on beside the hand-me-down kit. Its picture fills the CRT over by the couch.

Songs.Title: bad guy
Songs.PlayingNote: The clipped verse groove gives way to a much heavier, slower-feeling coda.

Cue.Do: The CRT is turned toward the kit now. In its glass the drummer can watch the take while playing. The red lamp stays on.

Songs.Title: February Air
Songs.PlayingNote: The electronic backbeat carries across the rising synth chorus.

Cue.Do: Daylight in the window well fades to streetlamp blue. A rectangle of kitchen light opens at the top of the stairs.

Songs.Title: Sleeping In - Remastered
Songs.PlayingNote: The repeating electronic beat keeps its place under the softer vocal phrases.

Cue.Do: Light reaches down another stair. Someone upstairs has propped the kitchen door open to hear the take.

Songs.Title: Fireflies
Songs.PlayingNote: The beat fills out under the chorus and pulls back under the verse.

Cue.Do: The CRT holds the last frame of the take. A crate with the old orange bucket and sticks now waits in the kitchen light at the foot of the stairs.

Reward.Name: Busking crate
Reward.Placement: under the stairs beside the orange bucket
Reward.Description: A milk crate just big enough for the bucket, sticks and phone speaker. It waits under the basement stairs. Turn it over at the station and you have a drum throne.

Sets.Title: The Last Train Busking Pitch
Sets.VenueWork: Build the tiled platform edge, pillar, stairs and departure board around the compact stage. Pass a light rig behind carriage-shaped flats for each train.
Sets.KitLook: Orange bucket and practice pad on the upturned crate
Sets.Premise: A phone speaker, a bucket and a dry patch between the turnstiles and the stairs. Two trains will come and go before the commuter in the mustard scarf spends their first loonie.

Songs.Title: We Will Rock You - Remastered 2011
Songs.PlayingNote: Two low hits and one sharp clap give the crowd the whole figure.

Cue.Do: One mustard scarf stops under the departure board. A steel mug catches the light as the commuter bobs to the two stomps and clap.

Songs.Title: Clint Eastwood
Songs.PlayingNote: The same loping beat has to last through a long verse.

Cue.Do: Lit carriage windows sweep past the pillar. When the light clears, the commuter and mug are still beside the kit.

Songs.Title: Paper Planes
Songs.PlayingNote: The sparse backbeat leaves the chorus sound effects exposed.

Cue.Do: Two kids join the patch of light. They throw both hands up on the hook while their mum watches from the stairs.

Songs.Title: Please Mr. Postman
Songs.PlayingNote: A quick Motown backbeat carries the handclaps under the call and answer.

Cue.Do: A second train takes its windows’ reflection with it. Mum has joined the children by the bucket and is clapping.

Songs.Title: I Want You Back
Songs.PlayingNote: The bright snare holds the backbeat against a much busier bass line.

Cue.Do: The scarf bobs above the dancers. After the cutoff, hold on the open case with the drilled loonie and a café transfer laid across the lining.

Reward.Name: First tip and café transfer
Reward.Placement: loonie on the hi-hat stand and the handwritten transfer on the board
Reward.Description: Hang the drilled loonie from the hi-hat stand. Back in the basement, pin the handwritten café transfer to the gig board.

Sets.Title: The Millennial Coffee Shop
Sets.VenueWork: Push the audience close on three sides. A working counter, steam cue and two tables make the room read in a single wide.
Sets.Premise: The manager pays in cash and a breakfast sandwich. Jules from the early shift sits in on guitar for the one-minute opener. The rest of the set runs from the backing track while Jules pulls shots. Two customers share a table, a laptop and a very good excuse to stay.

Songs.Title: Ramona - Acoustic Version
Songs.PlayingNote: The one-minute acoustic take leaves the guitar pulse exposed. Use its rests.

Cue.Do: The barista plays the opener in an apron, then puts the guitar on a stand by the till. The foil-wrapped breakfast sandwich keeps the setlist flat.

Songs.Title: Cactus In The Valley - Acoustic
Songs.PlayingNote: The two voices trade lines over gentle acoustic phrasing.

Cue.Do: The barista is back at the counter. On the nearest two-top, an open laptop drops to half mast and the duet can see both faces above it.

Songs.Title: Kiss Me
Songs.PlayingNote: The verse lilt opens up on the chorus backbeat.

Cue.Do: Two chairs now face the kit. A backpack appears under a table, leaving one spare chair in the warm pool of stage light.

Songs.Title: Stolen Dance
Songs.PlayingNote: The same lilting groove has to hold for more than five minutes.

Cue.Do: The empty chair has an occupant. Three pairs of knees sway together in the aisle while steam rises in clouds behind the bar.

Songs.Title: Little Talks
Songs.PlayingNote: The beat stays buoyant beneath the alternating voices and shouted answers.

Cue.Do: At the shouted response, the steam cuts out. The barista claps over the counter and the seated customers answer. An untouched cup waits on the pass.

Reward.Name: House brushes in an espresso tin
Reward.Placement: on the practice bench by the gig board
Reward.Description: Take home the house brushes in a stained espresso tin. They fit on the basement practice bench beside the gig board.

Sets.Title: The Dead End Dive Bar
Sets.VenueWork: Share the Legion’s small hall footprint. Use the back-bar mirror, green pool light and table cover to show who stays after the match.
Sets.Premise: Your new bassist wedges an amp against your knees. The bartender offers you the door take if you can keep the pool league around after the last game. You can count the entire audience in the mirror behind the bottles.

Songs.Title: Ain't No Rest For The Wicked
Songs.PlayingNote: The backbeat sits behind the swagger of the riff and the gaps at each line ending.

Cue.Do: Light the green felt at one edge of the stage. The pool league gathers around the scattered balls, backs to the band. Their reflections fill the bar mirror.

Songs.Title: The Garden
Songs.PlayingNote: The vocal exchanges leave room for short drum answers.

Cue.Do: One league shirt appears at the stage end of the bar. A cue leans against the stool while the shooter watches the singers’ end of the room.

Songs.Title: Paralyzer
Songs.PlayingNote: The kick follows the clipped dance riff beneath a square backbeat.

Cue.Do: The eight ball disappears from the felt. The racked balls for the rematch wait in the return while two more league shirts start moving to the riff.

Songs.Title: Icky Thump
Songs.PlayingNote: Kick and crash accents follow the uneven lengths of the guitar phrases.

Cue.Do: The green rectangle becomes a dark table cover. Cues hang in the rack and a row of pints catches the light along its edge.

Songs.Title: Are You Gonna Be My Girl
Songs.PlayingNote: The tambourine pickup, band entrance and sudden stops have to line up.

Cue.Do: The league claps through the stops. At the cutoff the mirror catches the bartender beside a bulging door envelope, with the covered table visible behind them.

Reward.Name: Threadbare drum rug and garage key
Reward.Placement: under the kit with the key on a hook by the door
Reward.Description: The door take pays for a garage key. Move the band into the garage, hang the key by the door and unroll the bar’s threadbare rug under the kit. The old kick-spur holes still line up.

Sets.Title: Funeral Afterparty at the Legion
Sets.VenueWork: Redress the bar footprint with a strip of parquet, folding chairs, a dessert table on wheels and an upright piano.
Sets.KitLook: Legion kit with a tea towel on the snare
Sets.Premise: Dad asked for the Beatles. His daughter brought the mix she made for the ride home. Leave a square of parquet for her first dance. Her uncle thinks he’s just here to make the toast.

Songs.Title: While My Guitar Gently Weeps - Remastered 2009
Songs.PlayingNote: Keep the kit in view as the drummer settles into Dad’s record.

Cue.Do: From behind the kit, find the uncle holding his toast card and the daughter beside Dad’s empty chair. She mouths the guitar phrase. End on the uncle’s wet shoulder.

Songs.Title: A Place Where You Belong
Songs.PlayingNote: Give the opening to the pallbearers and return to the kit for the lead guitar.

Cue.Do: Track beside the casket at shoulder height through the rain. Widen to the black umbrellas at the grave. As the casket lowers, its lid clears the daughter’s sightline to Dad’s friends opposite. Back at the Legion, the cousins wheel the dessert table aside.

Songs.Title: Cure for the Enemy
Songs.PlayingNote: Start behind the kit with the cleared parquet beyond the cymbals.

Cue.Do: Dad’s friend comes in wearing the same rain-dark suit she carried him in. Her wife eases the jacket off her shoulders. Across the floor the daughter has left her shoes by the empty chair and taken her uncle’s hands.

Songs.Title: I’ll Be Late For My Funeral
Songs.PlayingNote: Let the drummer’s accents draw the family onto the floor.

Cue.Do: Dad’s portrait now faces the dancers from the upright piano. The uncle’s tie is draped over its corner and a little stack of napkin requests has appeared.

Songs.Title: Helena
Songs.PlayingNote: The quiet entrance breaks into fast, driving drums, with sharp changes back to space.

Cue.Do: The cousins fill the parquet on the full-band rush. His shoes join hers by the chair. At the cutoff a photo flash catches the whole family beneath Dad’s portrait.

Reward.Name: The request slip wrapped around a family photo
Reward.Placement: pinned to the wall above the kit
Reward.Description: The daughter folds her request slip around the photo of the cousins dancing. Pin both over the garage kit.

Sets.Title: Adults Only at the Roller Rink
Sets.VenueWork: Add an oval lane, rail and booth. Three featured skaters travel on repeatable paths under a single mirror ball.
Sets.KitLook: Compact disco kit behind the DJ booth
Sets.Premise: Somebody carried the nacho warmer downstairs so you could fit the kit in the booth. The regulars in silver jackets know every turn on this floor. The last pair of orange rentals went to somebody who has never made a lap.

Songs.Title: Daddy Cool
Songs.PlayingNote: Kick and bass carry the steady disco pulse.

Cue.Do: Two silver jackets circle the centre while a pair of orange rentals stays at the rail. Light the jackets together and leave the rail in the house light.

Songs.Title: Can't Get You out of My Head
Songs.PlayingNote: A straight dance pulse makes small changes in hat articulation audible.

Cue.Do: On the hook, a second pool of light picks out the orange rentals. Each lap now brings the silver pair back through both pools.

Songs.Title: Gimme! Gimme! Gimme! (A Man After Midnight)
Songs.PlayingNote: The offbeats sit above the steady kick under the repeated synth hook.

Cue.Do: The mirror ball starts turning. At the next wide the rail is empty and the orange rentals have made it onto the inside lane.

Songs.Artist: Daft Punk, Pharrell Williams, Nile Rodgers
Songs.Title: Get Lucky (feat. Pharrell Williams and Nile Rodgers)
Songs.PlayingNote: The pocket stays level for six minutes against the interlocking guitar and bass.

Cue.Do: The three skaters share one lap. Each time they pass the booth another pair has joined the line behind them.

Songs.Title: Treasure
Songs.PlayingNote: Short band accents interrupt the groove without losing the dance pulse.

Cue.Do: A circle opens under the mirror ball. The skater in orange reaches the middle upright and both silver jackets throw their hands in the air.

Reward.Name: Dented mirror ball
Reward.Placement: turning below the ceiling over the kit
Reward.Description: Take home the rink’s dented mirror ball. It casts a moving spot across the garage ceiling.

Sets.Title: The Pledge Drive Night Shift
Sets.VenueWork: Dress a studio as two rooms divided by glass. Five phone lights and large pledge cards carry the action behind the band.
Sets.Premise: A campus station loses its sampler on pledge night. You take the shift with five local voices rotating through one mic. On the other side of the glass, volunteers have until the end of the broadcast to make rent.

Songs.Title: Juicy - 2007 Remaster
Songs.PlayingNote: The sampled groove repeats under long, conversational verses.

Cue.Do: Across the control-room glass, one of five desk phones lights up. The first pledge slip appears on the pane level with the presenter’s head.

Songs.Title: Ms. Jackson
Songs.PlayingNote: The backbeat stays planted against the reversed-sounding accompaniment.

Cue.Do: A second phone lights at the other end of the desk. Two volunteers are up now, with a trail of paper starting between them.

Songs.Title: King Kunta
Songs.PlayingNote: The stops and clipped hats make room for the bass.

Cue.Do: Pledge sheets climb halfway up the glass. Through the top half, volunteers are on their feet bouncing to the bassline.

Songs.Title: Put Me Thru
Songs.PlayingNote: The drums answer the vocal in the gaps and settle straight back into the groove.

Cue.Do: All five phones glow. A hand-sized gap in the pledge slips frames the presenter swaying beside the vocal mic.

Songs.Title: Chicken Grease
Songs.PlayingNote: The laid-back snare rubs against a sharply clipped guitar pulse.

Cue.Do: A single RENT PAID sheet fills that gap. The volunteers jump on the far side of the soundproof pane. The band can see the cheer while the take rolls.

Reward.Name: Red ON AIR lamp and the session tape
Reward.Placement: lamp over the door and tape on the shelf
Reward.Description: Move into the rented rehearsal room. Wire the station’s red ON AIR lamp over the door and shelve the tape of your shift.

Sets.Title: Food Court Farewell Show
Sets.VenueWork: Dress the floor around a drained fountain and raised cafeteria tables. Closing shutters and a reversible signed head tell the farewell story.
Sets.KitLook: Touring kit on three cafeteria tables
Sets.Premise: The mall closes Sunday. On Saturday the skate shop spends the last of its promo money on your band’s first full-lineup matinee. Somebody has brought a marker and a spare kick head for the regulars to sign.

Songs.Title: Addicted
Songs.PlayingNote: A bouncing verse groove gives the chorus its lift.

Cue.Do: The spare white drumhead leans on the lip of the drained fountain with one black signature. The kid in the skate-shop hoodie claims the spot beside it.

Songs.Title: Sk8er Boi
Songs.PlayingNote: Straight eighths drive the fast vocal and the push into the chorus.

Cue.Do: Two boards stand beside the head. A broad cartoon of a peaked cap has appeared on it. The mall guard stands directly behind the two skaters.

Songs.Title: Fat Lip
Songs.PlayingNote: The beat switches cleanly between rapped phrases and the sung hook.

Cue.Do: The drumhead faces the camera again, now sporting a gigantic moustache under the cap. The guard claps beside the kid in the hoodie.

Songs.Title: Basket Case
Songs.PlayingNote: The drums enter after the opening guitar and carry the pulse through quick rolls.

Cue.Do: The last shop shutters roll down. Staff still in name tags fill the fountain rim, and the head comes back almost black with signatures.

Songs.Title: Misery Business
Songs.PlayingNote: Snare pickups, cuts and the return from the breakdown lead into the last chorus.

Cue.Do: The signed head stands on the drum riser after the cutoff. The kid points both arms up from the fountain as the crowd jumps around them.

Reward.Name: Food-court kick head
Reward.Placement: on the wall above the spare stands
Reward.Description: Hang the signed kick head over the spare stands in the rehearsal room. The skate-shop manager gets your kit onto the truck for the next out-of-town show.

Sets.Title: Midnight at the FM Drive In
Sets.VenueWork: Slope rows of parked cars toward a screen. Headlight banks, a reversible quilt prop and a stage feed sell the scale.
Sets.KitLook: Hybrid kit beside the projection booth
Sets.Premise: The regional electronic festival sends your kit out over FM. It’s your first booking away from town. A quilt and a battered hatchback mark the pair whose shadows will end up forty feet tall.

Songs.Title: Genesis
Songs.PlayingNote: The opening accents land far apart against the heavy synth pulse.

Cue.Do: The FM frequency fills the screen above the stage. The hillside of headlights comes on together. One hatchback faces backwards with its tailgate up.

Songs.Title: Promises
Songs.PlayingNote: A half-time snare stays steady beneath the rising synth line.

Cue.Do: Two people share a quilt in the open hatch. The neighbouring pickup switches on its cargo lamp and a thermos gleams between the vehicles.

Songs.Title: Scary Monsters and Nice Sprites
Songs.PlayingNote: The slow snare anchors the drop while the kick answers the chopped sounds.

Cue.Do: The quilt lies on the roof. Two silhouettes bounce in the gravel between the cars and cross the bottom of the projection screen.

Songs.Title: Omen
Songs.PlayingNote: The breakbeat pushes forward through the repeating hook.

Cue.Do: A whole patch of dancers finds the projector beam. Their raised arms cast giant silhouettes above the hatchbacks.

Songs.Title: Witchcraft
Songs.PlayingNote: The drum-and-bass pulse returns under the vocal and runs into the outro.

Cue.Do: A pair of sticks crosses the beam. The projection switches to the live kit feed and those two sticks become forty feet tall.

Reward.Name: Projectionist’s amber count-in lamp
Reward.Description: Back in the rehearsal room, the projectionist’s amber lamp signals the count-in from beside the PA.

Sets.Title: One Night on the Steel Mill Tour
Sets.VenueWork: Enclose the festival stage in rolling-mill girders. Keep the lit changeover wing and the labelled road case visible on wides.
Sets.Premise: A metal package tour needs one drummer for five changeovers. Each act gets one song with you and leaves a marked-up sheet by the floor tom. Halfway through the night, the crew stops clearing the wing. The other bands want to see this.

Songs.Title: This Could Be Anywhere In The World
Songs.PlayingNote: The opening drum figure has to establish the pulse before the voices enter.

Cue.Do: The first set sheet is taped to the riser. The opener’s singer walks to the mic on the drum entrance. Bare mill girders frame the crowd behind them.

Songs.Title: Collapsing
Songs.PlayingNote: Short kick bursts lock to the guitar chugs.

Cue.Do: A blue sheet joins the first. The opening act’s bass player stays in the wing with a towel around their neck. The next act takes the lights.

Cameos.Do: The barista watches the second act from beside a bass case with a café sticker.
Ness stands with the first act’s bass tech under the wing light, white strap on the case.

Songs.Title: Duality
Songs.PlayingNote: Toms and snare trade accents over the low guitar pulse.

Cue.Do: Three sheets now face the house. The first two acts watch the tom accents from the wing, with a roll of tape perched on the monitor.

Songs.Title: Bat Country
Songs.PlayingNote: The fast subdivision continues under the guitar lead and through the fills.

Cue.Do: A work lamp comes on beyond the fourth set sheet. Under it sits a road case with a fresh stencil, still turned away from the crowd.

Songs.Title: Scream Aim Fire
Songs.PlayingNote: Sustained fast kicks and thrash accents close the shift on the house kit.

Cue.Do: After the cutoff, all five singers come out beside the five sheets. The case turns into the work light so the name on it reads from the back rows.

Reward.Name: Road case with five bands’ tape
Reward.Placement: beside the load-out door with the stencil facing out
Reward.Description: The tour crew leaves you the case with five bands’ tape on it. Park it by the rehearsal room’s load-out door with your name facing out.

Sets.Title: Home Ice at Maple Leaf Gardens
Sets.VenueWork: Bring the riser to centre ice. Dress the boards, goal lamps and rafters as the old hockey palace and rig a banner that can unfurl.
Sets.KitLook: Tour kit on a centre-ice riser
Sets.Premise: Maple Leaf Gardens, dressed for a dream booking in the old hockey-palace configuration. Five Canadian records. For the first time the promoter asks what your band wants to play. The first goal lamp comes on at soundcheck. By the encore you can see your name in the rafters.

Songs.Title: Gold Guns Girls
Songs.PlayingNote: The repeating drive leaves little space to recover between choruses.

Cue.Do: A red goal lamp picks out a kid at the glass in an enormous sweater, bouncing beside the centre-ice riser.

Cameos.Do: Rory claps beside the opener’s sunburst guitar at the home bench.
The opener’s seafoam guitar rests next to Bea at the home bench.

Songs.Title: Trainwreck 1979
Songs.PlayingNote: The exposed bass and drum hits have to land together.

Cue.Do: Goal lamps at opposite ends of the rink trade light across the stage. The kid throws both sleeves up on the unison hits.

Songs.Title: This Suffering
Songs.PlayingNote: Clipped guitar phrases leave the drummer to mark the turnarounds.

Cue.Do: A wave of raised arms starts at the sweater and runs along the glass to the players’ bench.

Cameos.Do: Kit waves from the visitors’ bench in the opening act’s jacket.
Sol sways beside the opener’s honey-coloured mic at the visitors’ bench.

Songs.Title: Masterpiece Theatre III
Songs.PlayingNote: Returning themes ask for several distinct entrances across a long suite.

Cue.Do: Above centre ice a follow spot finds a furled banner going up by its ropes. A loose corner hangs into the light through the final chord.

Cameos.Do: Dee is at the opener’s keys rack under a blue lamp.
Otto listens beside the opener’s organ at the home tunnel.

Songs.Title: Tom Sawyer
Songs.PlayingNote: The instrumental changes metre, then the fills have to resolve back into the main groove.

Cue.Do: At the end of the fills the sweater sleeves fly up again. On the last hit the banner unfurls with the band’s name facing the cheap seats.

Reward.Name: Miniature rafter banner
Reward.Placement: over the mixing desk with the band name and date
Reward.Description: Move the band into the studio. A miniature of the rafter banner hangs over the mixing desk, complete with your band name and the date.

Sets.Title: The Retractable Roof Is Open
Sets.VenueWork: Open the Arena roof and extend the upper bowl. Two side screens give people in the last row a clear view of the loonie and the bucket.
Sets.KitLook: Headline kit with the subway bucket beside the floor tom
Sets.Premise: At your hometown headline, the same bucket sits next to the floor tom. You get almost half an hour under an open roof. Leave breath between the big entrances. By the time the long guitar coda arrives, the crowd knows what to play back.

Songs.Title: Baba O'Riley
Songs.PlayingNote: The drum entrance locks to the repeating synth. Save room to drive the fiddle-led finish.

Cue.Do: The side screen finds a mustard scarf and the dented mug at the barricade. A whole stand claps the old bucket pattern before the camera widens on the synth entrance.

Songs.Title: Welcome to the Black Parade
Songs.PlayingNote: A patient opening gives way to marching snare and the double-time charge.

Cue.Do: Phones light the upper deck from one end to the other. When the marching snare enters, pairs of lights begin descending the aisles.

Songs.Title: Bohemian Rhapsody - Remastered 2011
Songs.PlayingNote: Long vocal passages give the hands a breather. The hard part is counting the heavy re-entry.

Cue.Do: Opposite stands take opposite sides of the operatic exchange, each on its own screen. Both screens cut to the band on the heavy return.

Songs.Title: Everlong
Songs.PlayingNote: Rapid hats stay even while kick placements and section accents change beneath them.

Cue.Do: Hold the kit close-up through the fast hats. The frame widens to the drilled loonie swinging on its stand, big enough for the upper deck to see.

Songs.Title: Free Bird
Songs.PlayingNote: The quiet first half leaves a reserve for the extended, accelerating guitar coda.

Cue.Do: The last hit dies away under the open roof. The stand gives back the bucket pattern, the drummer answers on the bucket, and the mug goes up one last time.

Reward.Name: Framed hometown headline ticket
Reward.Placement: beside the first loonie after load-out
Reward.Description: Frame the hometown headline ticket beside the first loonie in the studio. Credits roll over the load-out, and the last shot is the battered bucket going back in the van. After the credits, the next booking on the board bears the seal of the Drummer Hall of Fame.

Sets.Title: The Drummer Hall of Fame at the Event Horizon
Sets.VenueWork: Turn the upper bowl into an orbital rotunda. Hang five concentric brass rings above the band against a star field. Put the black disc, the bent starlight and the engraved names high above the highway. Keep one plain music stand and one warm rehearsal lamp beside the kit.
Sets.KitLook: The touring kit with five brass contact pickups and the drilled loonie on the hat stand
Sets.Premise: Your induction concert is already on the air when a black hole starts eating the stars outside the Hall. The orbital station has five brass rings around its hull. The kit is wired to their drive coils. Every strike sends a pulse out through the metal. Across the stage, the house conductor lifts a baton. Your band watches you.

RunPolicy.Description: Start at track one and play straight through the final cutoff. Run the original recordings end to end. Each ending feeds the next opening automatically, with a continuous stage feed and a single results screen after song five. Leaving the gig, closing the game or restarting a song ends the attempt. Start the next attempt at track one with fresh scores and rings. Pass on the mean accuracy of these five performances.

Songs.Title: Good Times Bad Times - 1993 Remaster
Songs.PlayingNote: The right foot slips quick doubles underneath an unhurried backbeat. Let the upper body look relaxed enough that the conductor could read the tempo from your shoulders.

Cue.Do: The first brass ring turns edge-on to the hole. Reflected light runs around it on the kicks. The conductor lowers the baton to hear where the snare lands.

Songs.Title: Assassin
Songs.PlayingNote: The opening attack goes straight from the wrists into the whole kit. Place the busy snare and tom figures cleanly enough that the band can hit the next unison accent with you.

Cue.Do: The second ring snaps into line on the opening figure. Through the gap between rings, a row of stars appears twice as its light bends around the black disc. The bassist locks eyes with the drummer.

Songs.Title: Lateralus
Songs.PlayingNote: Carry the riff through its groups of nine, eight and seven. Give the band a downbeat it can trust when the phrase turns over, then hold enough in reserve for the long build.

Cue.Do: The third ring sweeps across the doubled stars. Its shadow passes the music stand at a different point in each phrase. The band stays together as the conductor steps back from the stand.

Songs.Title: Contact
Songs.PlayingNote: Build the rolling snare and cymbals against the repeating synth. As the distortion swallows the attack, keep subdividing all the way through the noise tail into the next tune.

Cue.Do: The fourth ring glows white. The black disc fills the windows until the musicians can see only one another under the rehearsal lamp. The conductor turns to the drummer for the next entrance.

Songs.Title: What About Me?
Songs.PlayingNote: The funk figure gives everyone a common pulse. Keep it audible through the displaced accents, make a phrase out of the drum feature, and give the ensemble a clear way back in. After twenty-two minutes on the kit, the last skill is listening.

Cue.Do: The horns come up over the Hall speakers. The fifth ring turns above the kit. Hold the shot on the drummer through the exposed figures, then widen to catch the whole band taking the closing hits from the sticks.

Reward.Name: Engraved induction stand
Reward.Placement: beside the practice pad, open to the first page
Reward.Description: The rings strike together on your cutoff. Their returning pulse pinches the black hole shut. Stars reappear through its centre. In the silence, the conductor lays the baton across the snare and turns your music stand around. Its brass face now carries your name beside the other inductees. Your band carries it home to the studio as an epilogue.

ProposedSets.Title: Highway to the Afterlife
ProposedSets.Premise: Five songs follow one band from a highway chase to an audience with God. On Earth, the whole trip takes only as long as the rescue.

Songs.Title: Kickstart My Heart
Songs.PlayingNote: Straight-ahead speed: keep the double-time hi-hat driving and land the stops clean.

Cue.Do: The trailer slews across the lane, crashes and erupts in flame. The helicopter holds wide on the fire.

Moments.Do: Low on a trailer wheel against the lane markings, rising past the flatbed's edge to the kick pedal.
Head-on through the cruiser's windshield: the cop's eyes on the trailer.
The helicopter: wide on both vehicles, then the operator zooms past the trailer and corrects back onto the drummer.
On the deck: a band member braces a foot against a monitor.
The cop checks his radio.
One small involuntary nod in time.
The helicopter again, both vehicles in frame.
In the closing bars the trailer slews across a lane; the last hits with the kit still in view.
Road level: the band lies on the asphalt, one drumstick just beyond the drummer's fingers. Held into Free Bird.

Songs.Title: Free Bird
Songs.PlayingNote: Breathe through the slow opening, then hold the tempo as the jam gathers speed into the solo.

Cue.Do: The crowd turns to the throne. Satan rolls one hand toward the band for another song.

Moments.Do: Beside the drummer's hand on the road as the recording starts.
Wide: both versions of the band, the ghosts standing over their bodies.
The cop runs from the cruiser to the drummer's body.
The cop runs in and kneels beside the drummer's body.
The road falls away: ash floats up, then they realise they are falling. The road overhead shrinks to a bright slit.
Tumbling past one another, pulling back into their places.
The kick drum hits stone at the foot of a staircase.
Up the stairs past the demons on the balustrades to Satan on the throne.
Along the shoulder past the cruiser and its lights to the burning rig: the whole scene before anyone moves.
Straight up from among the falling band: the road a slit of light, shrinking.
High over the lake of lava: the island, the terraces of demons, the stairs and the skull over the throne.

Songs.Title: Bat Country
Songs.PlayingNote: Swing the shuffle, and give every fill an ending Satan can follow.

Cue.Do: Satan picks up a phone beside the throne and looks straight up: “You gotta hear these guys.”

Moments.Do: From the throne looking down on the stage.
A demon on the steps catches a fill with both hands on the stone, then turns to see whether Satan noticed.
Satan head-on, the cop's distance: nodding along.
Satan finishing the fill on the armrests.
By the closing passage he is on his feet.

Moments.Caption: “You gotta hear these guys.”
Moments.Do: Satan, into the phone, looking straight up.
His free hand lifts; the drummer's boots leave the stone and smoke rises past the lens, turning white.
Round the back of the band, low: the kit against the crowd, the stairs and the throne beyond.

Songs.Title: Stairway to Heaven
Songs.PlayingNote: Wait out the quiet opening; when the drums come in, play it big and patient under the choir.

Cue.Do: As the performance resolves, the angels turn toward the drummer. God waits on the platform.

Moments.Do: Inches from the side of the drummer's face, cloud and the others drifting in and out of focus.
Another member looking down for the friend who fell beside them; their eyes meet.
The first view of the horizon.
The highway is back; the camera pulls back as the band touches down on a floor of cloud.
The distant arch opens its eyes: rings and wings, then a whole choir of angels, the band small at the bottom of the frame.
From the celestial wide all the way back to a close shot of the sticks.
Far back and high: the band a speck on its dais, the gates, the platform and the whole choir.

Songs.Title: My Hero
Songs.PlayingNote: The exposed opening is all yours: keep the toms even and let the guitars land on you.

Cue.Do: Back on the shoulder at normal speed: the drummer opens their eyes, an EMS worker sees another band member stir.

Moments.Do: Tight on the drummer in heaven through the opening pattern.
Match cut on a stick stroke: the cop's hands giving CPR on Earth, slow motion, the trailer still burning, red and blue across his face.
Earth wide: the cop in the foreground, the flashing light leading back to the responders around the others.
The cop's attention stays on the person in front of him.
Final chorus: God comes down the stairs to the band's level.
The angels fold their wings aside; through the opening, the crash site.
Two fingers tapping the asphalt. The cop hears it and gives the same small nod. End of the set.

ProposedSets.Staging: One continuous show (Continuous): each song's tail plays into the next recording with no results screen until My Hero ends. One sitting for now: leaving starts over at the chase. Each song names its venue; flags land at their cues (Cue and Moments), and a camera spot tagged story/<flag> in the venue takes the screen when its flag lands. Cue times are placeholders (at:<share>, last_note+N) until the charts have sections. Flags starting band_ move the live band and are each song's own (they never carry to the next): band_ghost (see-through, glowing), band_down (on their backs), band_falling (tumbling), band_floating, band_rising (lifted off the floor), band_hidden, band_playing (back at their marks); the latest pose wins, blended over 2.5 s. A moment can carry a Caption: a line shown on screen.

Auditions.Scene: Back at the basement board, two tear-off tabs are missing from BASSIST WANTED. Jules brings the café amp. Ness puts a strip of white tape on the floor where the kick creeps. Play the chorus with each.

Candidates.Name: Jules Park
Candidates.Personality: Counts under their breath and always leaves space for the singer.
Candidates.Signature: Café apron hanging off the amp
Candidates.Pitch: You saw what I can do in a minute. Give me a whole side.
Candidates.ReturnScene: The barista watches the second act from beside a bass case with a café sticker.

Candidates.Name: Ness Caron
Candidates.Personality: Says very little before a take and remembers every kick placement after it.
Candidates.Signature: White tape across the bass strap
Candidates.Pitch: Play me the bit you keep missing. That’s where my line goes.
Candidates.ReturnScene: Ness stands with the first act’s bass tech under the wing light, white strap on the case.

Auditions.Scene: The first night in the garage, use the dive-bar rug to mark out the space for a third player. Both candidates get the same stop on the same riff.

Candidates.Name: Rory Bell
Candidates.Personality: Takes the first run too fast, laughs, then nails the stop with the drummer.
Candidates.Signature: Sunburst guitar and a frayed strap
Candidates.Pitch: Give me one nod for the cut. The bar won’t hear the end coming.
Candidates.ReturnScene: Rory claps beside the opener’s sunburst guitar at the home bench.

Candidates.Name: Bea Okafor
Candidates.Personality: Patient enough to try six chord voicings until the snare has room.
Candidates.Pitch: If you can still hear your ghost notes, I’ve got the right chord.
Candidates.ReturnScene: The opener’s seafoam guitar rests next to Bea at the home bench.

Auditions.Scene: The rink lets two singers try the same chorus after closing. One sings toward the empty bleachers. One turns around to hear the band.

Candidates.Name: Kit Alvarez
Candidates.Personality: Can coax the one shy voice at the back of a room into the chorus.
Candidates.Pitch: Give me that last bar again. This time let them sing it.
Candidates.ReturnScene: Kit waves from the visitors’ bench in the opening act’s jacket.

Candidates.Name: Sol Baptiste
Candidates.Personality: Listens through the whole groove before choosing a place to come in.
Candidates.Pitch: You already put a breath there. I’ll sing on the other side of it.
Candidates.ReturnScene: Sol sways beside the opener’s honey-coloured mic at the visitors’ bench.

Auditions.Scene: At load-out the drive-in offers a spare power strip. Invite one keys player into the rehearsal room, or take the Gardens date as a four-piece.

Candidates.Name: Dee Lau
Candidates.Personality: Can hold one chord patiently until a room starts to move around it.
Candidates.Signature: Small keyboard with a blue lamp
Candidates.Pitch: You keep the clock. I’ll make the roof feel higher.
Candidates.ReturnScene: Dee is at the opener’s keys rack under a blue lamp.

Candidates.Name: Otto Klein
Candidates.Personality: Taps out odd metres on the bench and waits for the band to find beat one.
Candidates.Signature: Organ stool padded with an old scarf
Candidates.Pitch: I only need one outlet. Two if you want the organ to behave.
Candidates.ReturnScene: Otto listens beside the opener’s organ at the home tunnel.

Characters.Name: Mustard-scarf commuter
Characters.Signature: Mustard scarf and steel travel mug

Characters.Name: Dad’s daughter
Characters.Signature: Good shoes left beside her chair

Characters.Name: Hall conductor
Characters.Signature: Ivory baton and a brass music stand
